title: the README demo shows a user's Claude Code session, not the plugin's internals
description: The current GIF is drawn from Python: audit-status.py and a hand-fed PreToolUse payload, with typed captions standing in for the user. No user runs those scripts; they use Claude Code and /audit commands. The recording must show that experience while keeping the property the old one had: a check that fails when the words shown stop being the words the gate prints.
desiredOutcome: the demo GIF is a recording of a real Claude Code session in which the user types /audit commands and the plan gate refuses an edit the plan does not cover, with no personal data in any frame, and CI still fails when the refusal's words drift from what the gate prints

tasks.title: the demo GIF is a recorded Claude Code session with /audit commands and a real refusal
tasks.description: Replace the drawn demo with a recording of a real Claude Code session, made with VHS (installed: vhs 0.12.1, ttyd, ffmpeg) from a committed tape file. The session runs the real `claude` CLI in a demo project built fresh from the existing fixture (the same plan the current GIF shows: a running phase whose task owns src/checkout.ts), with this checkout's plugin loaded through --plugin-dir and an isolated --settings file whose allow list covers exactly the plugin's own commands' script calls, so no permission prompt interrupts and no permission bypass mode is shown. On screen the user types /audit:status and sees the plan; then asks Claude to change src/checkout.ts, which the plan covers, and it goes through; then asks for a change to src/billing.ts, which no task covers, and Claude Code shows the plan gate's refusal as it renders a PreToolUse deny. No frame may show personal data: no user name, email, organisation, machine name, home path or account banner; the project path on screen is a neutral demo path, never one under a home directory or this repo's scratch area. The recording also writes VHS's text output, and the sidecar record in docs/screenshots/captured-at.json (under the existing gifs key) keeps the GIF's sha256, the CLI version and model recorded, and the refusal text as recorded. tools/capture-demo-gif.py --check, which CI runs, keeps its guarantee without a paid session: it rebuilds the fixture, feeds require-plan the same out-of-plan payload, and fails when the gate's refusal text differs from the text the recording captured, or when the committed GIF's sha256 differs from the record. The drawn renderer and its Pillow dependency go, unless something still needs them. README's caption, CONTRIBUTING's re-record instructions (vhs, a logged-in claude, the tape, and what a re-record costs) and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE's entry say what the GIF now is. The executor prepares the tape, the fixture builder, the check and the documents, and dry-runs everything that does not start a Claude session; the orchestrator makes the recording.

add: tools/capture-demo-gif.py: --check fails when the gate's refusal text differs from the text the recording captured, and passes when they agree
tools/capture-demo-gif.py: --check fails when the committed GIF's sha256 differs from the record, or the record is missing

outcome.technical:
The README demo is now a VHS recording of a real Claude Code session (CLI 2.1.292, model sonnet), recorded from the committed tape tools/demo-gate.tape by `python3 tools/capture-demo-gif.py --record`. The demo project is built fresh from the fixture in the standard layout (docs/audit/audit-plan.json, no config, fileIndex derived from the tasks' files with the plugin's own key function, and validated with the rules audit-task add runs), with this checkout's plugin loaded by --plugin-dir and an isolated --settings whose allow list is exactly the plugin commands' script calls, promptSuggestionEnabled and spinnerTipsEnabled false. Off camera the tape accepts workspace trust through Claude Code's own dialog without IS_DEMO (IS_DEMO skips the dialog without granting trust, and hooks do not load in an untrusted folder), exits, relaunches with IS_DEMO and types /audit:status. On camera: the plan, an allowed edit of src/checkout.ts, then a src/billing.ts write refused by require-plan, Claude's reading of the refusal, and the end state. The window (font 14, 1200x2050, rows re-derived with tput) holds the whole take, because VHS reads only the top rows of the buffer.
Guards in the recorder, each refusing a take by name: personal data (email and organisation from `claude auth status --json`, host user, machine name, git identity, any home path, this checkout's path; the plan line is allowed - see task note 1); the usage-limit screen (read from screens only, never the echoed tape); a screen that outgrew the window; placeholder narration; an edit shown with no hook payload tapped (hooks not loaded); a submitted prompt the tape never typed; digits in an on-camera prompt (a dialog would read them as a choice); the tape lint (TAPE_NEEDS). The Waits prove each state: the live, empty input box between its borders before every prompt, the turn start, the refusal, and an interrupted-or-done end. `--check`, which CI runs without a paid session, rebuilds the fixture, refuses a plan with validator findings, replays the recorded PreToolUse payload against require-plan and fails when the refusal text, the GIF's sha256 or the record in docs/screenshots/captured-at.json (gifs) disagree. README, CONTRIBUTING, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and CI describe the recording and its check.
Recording history: ten takes; takes 1-9 were refused by the guards above or failed safely (wait shape, header, trust, VHS top-rows read, an LSP-recommendation dialog that consumed a prompt - which installed typescript-lsp at user scope on the operator's machine, left for the operator - empty-box shape, fixture fileIndex, window height). Take 10 recorded: 1151 KB, 73 s, --check OK. Selftest 77/77 (rr, m, f, s, p, i, e, v, ts, ul, fx, sr, pr groups); redFirst proved for the TDD cases before implementation (36/41), later groups by mutation rows, each red.
outcome.descriptive: The demo animation in the README is now a recording of an actual Claude Code session using the /audit commands - the plan, an allowed edit, and the plan gate refusing an unplanned one - instead of a picture drawn from the plugin's internal scripts, and CI checks that the refusal it shows is still what the plugin says today.

notes.text: Header decision (2026-10-07, orchestrator, under the operator's standing instruction to run to completion): Claude Code's startup header is recorded as a user sees it. The documented recording mode, IS_DEMO (code.claude.com env-vars reference), hides the email and organisation name and deliberately keeps the model and plan line, so the recording shows "Sonnet 5.5 · Claude Team"; no documented setting hides that line or the logo. The personal-data scan refuses what IS_DEMO promises to hide (email, organisation name read from `claude auth status --json`), the host's user name, machine name and git identity, any home path, and this checkout's path. Whether the plan line counts as the "account banner" the description excludes is left to the operator's visual approval of the GIF before it is published.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: recorded through the real CLI with the plugin loaded, no personal data in reviewed frames (plan line allowed, note 1), --check green against the committed GIF; operator visual approval pending before publication

tasks.title: the first-contact commands find the manifest themselves, so Claude never narrates an unfilled placeholder
tasks.description:
A user's first commands make Claude narrate an internal placeholder. In a recorded session with the manifest at the default docs/audit/audit-plan.json, /audit:status made Claude say "The command needs a manifest path that wasn't filled in, so I'll look for one" and "The command didn't fill in <manifestPath>, so I used the only manifest in the repo". Cause: status.md, usage.md, report.md and next.md hand the model a script line carrying a literal `<manifestPath>` to substitute, and a thin command does not read orchestrator.md, where the default is stated. The model has to guess, and it says that it guessed.

Fix it in code:
1. One shared resolver answers where the manifest is: the explicit argument, else `.claude/audit.config.json`'s manifestPath, else docs/audit/audit-plan.json. audit-usage.resolve_manifest_path already implements that rule; audit-task.py and panel-server.py hold copies of it.
   - Put the resolver in the lowest shared layer every caller can import, with its layer placement and guide section.
   - Route audit-usage through it.
2. audit-status.py and render-report.py take the manifest argument as optional and resolve it through the same resolver. When none is found, they say which places they looked.
3. status.md, usage.md, report.md and next.md drop `<manifestPath>` from their script lines. Every other line keeps working.
4. A drift check fails a thin command that hands the model a placeholder its script can resolve itself.

Out of scope, reported in the outcome with file:line: the orchestrator-driven commands that read orchestrator.md (phase, init, sync, propose, layout, task, bug, resume, doctor, worktree), and the audit-task and panel-server copies of the rule. A follow-up routes those through the resolver.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__manifest_io.py: the shared resolver answers the explicit argument, else the config's manifestPath, else docs/audit/audit-plan.json, and names the places it looked when none exists

plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_status.py: audit-status with no manifest argument renders the plan at the configured path and at the default path, and refuses with the looked-at places when there is none
plugins/audit/tests/test_render_report.py: render-report with no manifest argument renders the same report as with the resolved path
plugins/audit/tests/test__refs.py: a thin command whose script resolves the manifest itself carries no <manifestPath> placeholder, and the real status, usage, report and next commands pass

outcome.technical:
One resolver for where the manifest is: _manifest_io.resolve_manifest(project, explicit=None) answers the argument as given, else .claude/audit.config.json's manifestPath, else docs/audit/audit-plan.json, all relative to the project, and returns {path, source, looked, problem}; describe_unresolved names every place it looked. A config naming a missing or unreadable file is a refusal, never a fall-back to the default (that would render a different plan, with a different showCost, than the project points at); two old test_audit_usage cases pinning the fall-back are rewritten with the reason. The project is CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else the cwd (the rule audit-usage and render-report already used).
audit-usage.py: its own copy (resolve_manifest_path, DEFAULT_MANIFEST_REL) is gone; it calls the shared resolver, and when nothing resolves it still exits 0 but notes on stderr where it looked. audit-status.py and render-report.py take the manifest argument as optional and resolve it the same way; with none found they exit 2 with the shared refusal text. status.md, usage.md, report.md (three lines) and next.md no longer hand the model a `<manifestPath>` for a self-resolving script; status.md and report.md tell Claude to relay the refusal rather than search for a manifest.
Drift check: _refs.self_resolving_scripts() reads off the AST which scripts call <module>.resolve_manifest(...); _refs.manifest_placeholder_drift() reports any commands/*.md line handing one of them <manifestPath>, and any MANIFEST_PLACEHOLDER_PENDING row (phase.md, task.md, each with a reason) whose document no longer carries the placeholder. tools/prove-gates.py gains its red row (mp1, status.md re-given the placeholder), its allow row (the resolving-set filter dropped, which fires on status.md's verify-invariants line), and a NOT_A_GATE row for self_resolving_scripts; tools/gate-parity.py registers MANIFEST_PLACEHOLDER_PENDING as live under manifest_placeholder_drift.
Out of scope, recorded for a follow-up: placeholder lines in phase.md:110, task.md:171, orchestrator.md:92/102/723 and status.md:346 (verify-invariants does not resolve); copies of the rule in audit-task.py:96-97/1479 and _panel_paths.py:139; default constants in _journal_io.py:337, hooks/_config.py:153, _doctor_setup.py:773, _doctor_trail.py:944. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md sentences for the resolver, audit-usage and the lint go in a separate docs task after the sibling task commits the guide.
Tests: test__manifest_io rm1-rm8; test_audit_status mr1-mr5 (c3 now uses two positionals as its usage error); test_render_report rr-m1-rr-m3; test__refs mp1-mp6; test_audit_usage mn1, mn2. Red-first proved through the helper at HEAD b6d9a4a3 for all five files (mr1-mr5 and rr-m1-rr-m3 failing an assertion; the three --introduces runs failing at HEAD on the missing symbol and passing with the fix). Full sweep 305/305 files ok; prove-gates --selftest 37/37; gate-parity exit 0; ruff and vermin clean.
outcome.descriptive: /audit:status, /audit:usage, /audit:report and /audit:next now find the plan on their own and say where they looked when there is none, so Claude no longer tells the user it had to guess an unfilled placeholder.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: one shared resolver, three scripts resolve through it, four commands drop the placeholder, a drift lint with prove-gates rows in both directions keeps it from coming back; the remaining class is listed for a follow-up
